project_inclusion.note: Native to Texas according to Kew; retained here primarily for field relevance.

morphology_keys.leaves: Cordate-ovate to deltate-ovate, entire or 3(–5)-lobed; glabrous or sparsely hairy.
morphology_keys.sepals: Elliptic-oblong to lanceolate, usually 11–14 mm, ciliate, acuminate.
morphology_keys.corolla: Usually white, sometimes pink-tinged; about 15–20(–25) mm.
morphology_keys.key: Small white flower + 11–14 mm pointed sepals; compare with I. triloba and I. cordatotriloba.

field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: Small usually white corolla plus acuminate medium-length sepals. If it looks intermediate with tievine, consider the I. ×leucantha hybrid instead of forcing the ID.
fastest_traits: Sepals (8–)11–14 mm, acuminate, ciliate-margined and glabrous on the surfaces
Leaves entire or 3(–5)-lobed; lobing is not decisive

look_alikes.distinction: Both can be small-flowered; I. lacunosa is usually white and has longer acuminate sepals, whereas I. triloba sepals are typically about 6–7 mm.
I. cordatotriloba usually has a larger lavender flower and perennial habit, but hybridization produces intermediates.
FNA gives the hybrid a smaller 6–15(–20) mm corolla and 7–8 mm fruits; lacunosa fruits are 10–13 mm. FNA also reports lacunosa seeds 5–6 mm versus 3.2–4 mm in the hybrid.

hybrid_caution.note: This is a genuine identification trap in Texas/southeastern material; fruit and seed size become especially useful when flowers are intermediate.
